plumbing.name: 2021 International Plumbing Code with Fort Worth local amendments (Fort Worth City Code Chapter 26, Sections 26-1 and 26-2; Ordinance No. 25385-03-2022)
plumbing.quote: The Plumbing Code of the City of Fort Worth is hereby revised and amended to conform, with certain exceptions as specified below, to the 2021 International Plumbing Code and the 2021 International Fuel Gas Code of the International Code Council (ICC), and the same as amended are hereby adopted as the City's Plumbing Code. ... This ordinance shall take effect upon April 1, 2022.

codes.scheduled_change_note: The city's Building & Energy Codes page lists no 2024 editions and no adoption schedule. The 2022 council memo says Fort Worth "has historically adopted newly published Codes every six years" (2015 codes in 2016, 2021 codes in 2022).
codes.authority: City of Fort Worth Development Services Department (Building Official)

amendment.text: Fort Worth rewrote Sections 403.1, 403.2 and 403.3 of the plumbing code and did not change the ratios in Table 403.1. (1) The table counts are required, "based on the actual use of the building or space", and outside schools (Group E) the building official may approve fewer on a written request with reasons. (2) Separate men's and women's rooms are not required where the total occupant load, employees and customers together, is 50 or fewer (the model code says 15), in shops of 100 or fewer and in business occupancies of 25 or fewer; single-user toilet rooms need not be designated by sex. The rewritten exception list has no exception for multiple-user rooms designed for all genders. (3) Section 403.1.1 (half men, half women) and Section 424.2 (urinals in place of some water closets) are not amended; the city added only 424.3 (wall and floor finish around urinals) and 424.4 (waterless urinals). No urinals are required. Table footnote g and Sections 403.1.4 and 413.4 concern drinking fountains, food service sinks and floor drains.
amendment.quote: 403.1 Minimum number of fixtures. Plumbing fixtures shall be provided for the type of occupancy and in the minimum number shown in Table 403.1, based on the actual use of the building or space and as follows: ... Uses not shown in Table 403.1 shall be considered individually by the code official. The number of occupants shall be determined by the International Building Code. In other than E occupancies, the minimum number of fixtures in Table 2902.1 may be lowered, if requested in writing, by the applicant sating reasons for a reduced number and approved by the code official. || 403.2 Separate facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: 1. Separate facilities shall not be required for private dwelling units or sleeping units. 2. Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 50 or fewer. 3. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or less. 4. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer. 5. Separate facilities shall not be required to be designated by sex where single-user toilets rooms are provided in accordance with Section 403.1.2. 6. Self-service storage facilities need only provide one unisex restroom for storage tenant usage. ... 7. Aircraft T-hangar facilities need not install tenant restrooms when in compliance with the following: ...
amendment.pages: 9 to 12 of the ordinance (read as page images)

table_ratios.office: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50 (each sex)
table_ratios.urinals: none required; Section 424.2 lets urinals replace part of the men's water closets
table_ratios.source: Not read on a Fort Worth source: the ordinance does not reprint the table. Taken from research/state-codes/fixtures/dallas.json, which read the unamended 2021 IPC Table 403.1 rows on UpCodes.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Half the occupants counted as each sex, fractions rounded up. Same arithmetic as the Dallas examples (same unamended table); in Fort Worth the counts are required for all three uses, and reducible on written request except in schools. At 50 occupants separate rooms are not required (403.2 exception 2).

restrooms_city.rule: Fort Worth's plumbing code says single-user toilet rooms need not be designated by sex. Its rewritten list of exceptions to separate men's and women's facilities contains no exception for a shared multiple-user all-gender room. No separate city ordinance on restroom signs was looked for beyond the code amendments.
restrooms_city.quote: 5. Separate facilities shall not be required to be designated by sex where single-user toilets rooms are provided in accordance with Section 403.1.2.
restrooms_city.note: Section 403.1.2 itself is not amended by Fort Worth and was not read here. The building code's parallel section (2902.2) in Ordinance 25382-03-2022 was not read, so whether it also omits the all-gender exception is open.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Fort Worth job sites. Price your restroom, pick the right material and see the Fort Worth and Texas rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Fort Worth offices, schools, restaurants and distribution centers, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Fort Worth's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Fort Worth sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Fort Worth requires a permit to alter or repair a building unless the work is exempt. Its exempt list covers "similar finish work" and movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high, without naming toilet partitions, so ask Fort Worth Development Services whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom doesn't have to be designated for men or women. For larger restrooms, Fort Worth's plumbing rules call for separate men's and women's rooms and list no exception for a shared all-gender room, so ask Fort Worth Development Services before you plan one. Since December 2025, Texas law requires shared restrooms in city, county, school district and public college buildings to be designated for one sex.
page.stalls_intro: Fort Worth counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional and may stand in for some of the men's toilets. Outside schools, the city may approve fewer toilets if the applicant asks in writing and gives reasons.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building. Where a building or tenant space holds 50 people or fewer, staff and customers together, Fort Worth doesn't require separate men's and women's rooms. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or Fort Worth Development Services sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Anyone who obtains a Fort Worth building permit must have a contractor registration on file with the City. Texas has no statewide contractor license for this work. Confirm what your project needs with Fort Worth Development Services. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who obtains a Fort Worth building permit must be registered with the City.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on city, county and school district projects, Texas law requires at least the locally set wage. The federal rate for a carpenter on building work in Tarrant County is $15.47 an hour plus $1.82 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.25% in Fort Worth: 6.25% state, 1% city, 0.5% transit authority and 0.5% crime control district.
page.buyers_extra: - **Arenas, event halls and Stockyards venues:** HDPE or phenolic for restrooms that take big crowds and frequent washdown.
